main_text.l: terdum de pecuniis obligat . Sic in testamen-
to siquis Heres esto, vel Lego dixerit, maxi-
mas pecunias alienat. Sicverborum fuorum
Effecta Magi prædicant: cùm ex carminũ fuo-
rum euentis de vi verborum arguunt. Neque
ab hoc loco aliena sunt bona nomina, quæ
veteres notabant. Et Cicero in primo de Diui-
nat. Cùm Imperator (inquit) exercitum, Cen-
sor populum lustraret, bonis nominibus ; qui
hostias ducerent, eligebātur : quod item in de
leētu Consules obseruant, vt primus miles fiat
bono nomine.
Quid appellas Proprium dictionis? Pro-
prium dictionis, est vis vocabuli certa & nati-
ua, & penè (vt ait Cicero) cum ipsa re nata: ve-
luti Vagire proprium est infantium: plangere
fœminarum : vlulare canum : hinnire equo-
rum: rudere, asinorū: rugire leonum. Sic Or-
bus proprie dicitur, qui caret oculis. tranlatè
qui liberis, aut qui parentibus, aut qui alia
re chara priuatus est. Oracula (inquit Cicero)
ex eo ipso appellata sunt, quia inest in his deo-
rum oratio. Sic de Finib. 11. Varietas in dispa-
ribus coloribus proprie dicitur, sed transfer-
tur in plura disparia. Morbus proprie dicitur
in corpore: morbosos tamen veteres dicebant
iracundos. Proprie (inquit Cicero) vt Aegro-
tatio in corpore, sic Aegritudo in animo no-
men habet, non secundum à dolore. Et alibi:
Vnde iftud tam ἄχυρον[?], valetudini fideliter in-
seruiendo? cui verbo domicilium est proprium

page.notes: Catchword "in" at the foot right, excluded from the text. Running head printed with spaced capitals, given as DIALECTAE. Doubtful: the Greek word after "tam" reads as ἄχυρον but is marked [?]; "tranlatè" is printed without s and left as printed; "eligebātur" and "leētu" carry macron-like marks taken as printed; "Sicverborum" and "Effecta" are as printed. Long s normalised to s; "iftud" read with long s as "istud" is not changed (printed "iftud" kept as read: "iftud"). Small marks and dots at the lower edge are not printed text and are omitted.
